chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutaybah al-A'sha, who said:
'The mu'minah (female Believer) is more precious than the mu'min (male Believer), and the mu'min is more precious than red sulfur (al-kibrit al-ahmar). So who among you has (ever) seen red sulfur?'

key_terms.أَعَزُّ: More precious, rarer, more highly honored — an elative adjective conveying both extreme scarcity and supreme esteem simultaneously
key_terms.الْكِبْرِيتِ الْأَحْمَرِ: Al-kibrit al-ahmar (red sulfur): a legendary substance of near-mythical rarity in classical Islamic and Hermetic tradition, proverbially invoked for anything virtually impossible to find
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَةُ: The mu'minah: a female possessing complete and true iman (faith); here ranked as even more precious and rare than the mu'min
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: The mu'min: a male possessing complete and true iman (faith); used here to denote the genuine, fully realized believer
key_terms.رَأَى: Saw, witnessed, laid eyes upon — used in the rhetorical closing question to emphasize the near impossibility of ever encountering such a thing
key_terms.مِنْكُمُ: Among you — a direct address to the audience, making the rhetorical question personal and immediate

ai.seo_question: How rare is a true believer (mu'min) according to Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام), and why is the mu'minah considered even more precious?
ai.summary: Imam Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) declares that a true female believer (mu'minah) holds even greater honor and rarity than a male believer (mu'min), and that the mu'min himself is rarer and more precious than al-kibrit al-ahmar (red sulfur) — a legendary substance of unparalleled scarcity in classical Islamic and Hermetic tradition. The concluding rhetorical question — 'who among you has ever seen red sulfur?' — forcefully underscores that complete and genuine iman is exceedingly rare in the world, and that those who possess it are among the most singular of God's creation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Quteyba Al A’ash who said,
‘The Momina (female Believer) is more cherished than the Momin, and the Momin is more cherished than the alchemy. So who from you has (ever) seen alchemy?’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Qutaybah al-‘A’sha’ who has said the following:
‘The female believer is more valued than a male believer and a male believer is more valued than alchemy. Who among you has ever seen alchemy?’”
